Speculative decoding is a technique used to make large language models generate text faster. Instead of producing one word at a time, a smaller model first drafts several words ahead. The big model then checks that draft in a single pass, accepting the words it agrees with and correcting the ones it doesn't.

This works because verifying text is easier than creating it. The large model can review a whole chunk at once, so fewer slow passes are needed. Even if some guesses are wrong, the process still saves time because the big model only pays attention to what needs fixing.

In short, speculative decoding speeds up text generation by letting a small model guess ahead while the large model verifies those guesses in bulk.
